full_judgment:
Md. Ismailuddin Sarker, J.:- This Rule was issued upon an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure to show caws as to why the judgment and decree dated 13.13.83 of the Additional District Judge Kushtia in Title Appeal No. 76 of 1983 affirming those dated 24.5.83 of the First Court of Munsif at Kushtia in Title Suit No. 429 of 1981 should not be set aside. The plaintiff-petitioner instituted the suit on 17.12.81 against the defendant opposite parties for permanent injunction restraining opposite party No.1 from holding the examination of the Selection Board on 22.12.81 at Passkey for Selection of Grade 11 Station Masters. 

 4. The learned Munsif dismissed the suit on the finding that the suit was not maintainable in its present form because any decree if passed would be infructuous if the examination be shifted to a different date and a different place. The learned Munsif further held that the plaintiff-petitioner failed to show that he was promoted to Grade II Station Master. 

 5. On appeal, the learned Additional District Judge affirmed the judgment and decree of the Trial Court holding that the suit was not maintainable in its present form and that the petitioner's transfer order to Kushtia Station do not show that he was transferred on promotion to Grade II Station Master by that order. 

 6. In this suit the plaintiff petitioner claimed the following relief: "The plaintiff gets a decree for permanent injunction restraining defendant No.1 from holding selection board on 22-12-81 at Paksey as per his office order dated 548-E/SM/Grade III Selection." In view of the relief claimed in this suit the Courts below have rightly found that the suit was not maintainable. Moreover, the injunction sought for was to restrain the defendant No.1 from holding the examination on 22-12-81 and after the expiry of that date the suit became infractions much as the time for holding the examination has already expired during the pendency of the suit. Moreover, both the Courts below have found that the plaintiff failed to prove that he was posted at Kushtia on promotion to Grade II Station Master. In that view of the matter I find no ground to interfere with the Judgment and decree passed by the Courts below.
